title.narrative: [CONSORTIUM] Delivery of Integrated Lifesaving Services in Response to Displacement and Famine in Gedaref state.

description.narrative: ltpgtSince the outbreak of armed conflict in Sudan on April 15, 2023, and the fall of Al Gezira to RSF on December 15, 2023, as well as the recent fall of Sinja and the siege of Sennar, thousands of IDPs from these states are now hosted in Gadaref state. It is estimated that 851,964 individuals, or approximately 184,418 households, are affected. These internally displaced persons (IDPs) are accommodated in public facilities such as schools, mosques, shelters in markets, and within host communities. ltbrgtThe proposed multisector emergency lifesaving project integrates WASH, Protection, Cash for Shelter, and emergency shelter interventions to alleviate suffering among the conflict-affected population in Gedaref state. The shelter component will target 900 households in West Galabat, 760 HH in Wasat Gadaref, and 341 in Al Fashaga, providing cash-for-shelter assistance. In line with the conflict sensitivity approach, SORR will allocate 20% of its shelter component to the most vulnerable members of the host community, promoting peaceful coexistence between IDPs and hosts. The shelter component will use two approaches based on cluster recommendations: constructing shelters in government-designated locations for IDPs and providing shelter assistance to IDPs in host communities. ltbrgtThe WASH response will complement the shelter response by providing safe water, sanitation, hygiene promotion, and environmental campaigns across the three localities. In Wasat al Gedaref (total target: 1,650 households - 9,900 individuals), DRC will integrate the shelter response with WASH activities, including emergency water trucking, sustainable water supply, and maintenance. Hygiene kits and messaging will reach 500 households, and sanitation facilities will include 20 latrine blocks and 5 shower blocks. In Al Fashaga (1,500 households - 9,000 individuals), DRC will complement shelter programming with WASH NFIs (500 kits), intensive hygiene promotion, and cholera awareness. DRC will improve water sources and provide latrine cleaning tools, latrines, showers, and desludging services. In West Galabat (1,755 households, 10,530 individuals), DRC will support sites with lifesaving WASH services, including water trucking and long-term improvements. DRC will provide 650 hygiene kits and hygiene awareness campaigns. Emergency latrines will be constructed where dignified sanitation is lacking. ltbrgtTo build long-term capacity, DRC will conduct a capacity assessment and develop a plan to support WASH partners (especially local partners and government counterparts) and DRC staff in water system design, water quality testing, and hygiene behavior change. DRC will ensure community links for continued WASH services post-project, with a focus on behavior change through hygiene messaging. ltbrgtThe protection component aims to ensure access to a protective environment and basic services. In Al Fashaga, SORR target 5,000 individuals and will build the capacity of psycho-social service providers, provide dignity kits to GBV survivors, establish child protection networks, and protection monitoring. DRC will implement protection in Wasat Gedaref and West Galabat through mobile protection desks, community-based protection networks (CBPNs), Psychosocial First Aid, specialized referrals, protection awareness sessions, and individual protection assistance (IPAs). The response will include GBV and SEA mitigation through awareness sessions, dignity kits, and referrals. DRC's protection team will also provide training on general protection and sexual exploitation and abuse. Across Wasat Gedaref and West Galabat, 2,788 unique individuals will benefit from general protection activities, and 1,444 from GBV mitigationltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
